title.zh: 春秋战国：变革与百家争鸣

clips.send: Through conquest, seven powerful states remained in the Warring States period: Qi, Chu, Yan, Han, Zhao, Wei and Qin — the “Seven Warring States”. Rhyme: Qi east, Chu south, Qin west, Yan north, Zhao, Wei and Han in the middle.
clips.text: Through conquest, seven powerful states remained in the Warring States period: Qi, Chu, Yan, Han, Zhao, Wei and Qin — the “Seven Warring States”. Rhyme: Qi east, Chu south, Qin west, Yan north, Zhao, Wei and Han in the middle.

clips.send: Li Bing. Governor of Shu Commandery in the state of Qin. During the Warring States period (about 256 BCE), Li Bing, governor of Shu for the state of Qin, led the people in building Dujiangyan. It is one of the world’s oldest water projects still in use, and it works without a dam. It made Qin’s rear area rich, which helped Qin later unify China.

clips.send: Inner River (Neijiang). Carries water to the Chengdu Plain for irrigation. The Inner River bed is deeper and narrower. So in the dry season, when the water is low, more water flows into it — irrigation water is guaranteed. Watch the counter: in the dry season it takes about 60 percent.

clips.send: Chengdu Plain. “The Land of Abundance”. Before Dujiangyan, the plain often suffered both floods and droughts. After it, the plain could get water when it needed it and became “the Land of Abundance” (天府之国). Dujiangyan has worked for over 2,000 years and is a UNESCO World Heritage site (2000, with Mount Qingcheng).

clips.send: Memory rhyme: Where the seven states were: Qi east, Chu south, Qin west, Yan north, Zhao, Wei and Han in the middle. Order Qin conquered them: Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan, Qi.

clips.send: Outer River (Waijiang). The main river — carries the floods away. The Outer River bed is wider and shallower. In the flood season, when the water is high, most water (about 60 percent) rushes down the Outer River, so the plain is not flooded.

clips.send: From 230 to 221 BCE King Ying Zheng of Qin conquered the six states one by one — Han, Zhao, Wei, Chu, Yan, Qi — and in 221 BCE unified China. (You will meet the Qin dynasty in the next unit.)

clips.send: In 770 BCE King Ping moved east to Luoyi and the Eastern Zhou began. It has two parts: the Spring and Autumn period (770–476 BCE) and the Warring States period (475–221 BCE).
clips.text: In 770 BCE King Ping moved east to Luoyi and the Eastern Zhou began. It has two parts: the Spring and Autumn period (770–476 BCE) and the Warring States period (475–221 BCE).

clips.send: In the Spring and Autumn period the Zhou king grew weak and the lords fought to be “hegemon”. Duke Huan of Qi employed Guan Zhong to reform, rallied the lords with “honour the king, drive off the barbarians”, and became the first hegemon. Jin, Chu, Wu and Yue later competed too.

clips.send: In 356 BCE Duke Xiao of Qin backed Shang Yang’s reforms: private land could be bought and sold; farming and fighting were rewarded; ranks were given for military merit; counties were set up and run by officials sent by the ruler. Qin became the richest and strongest state of the late Warring States.

clips.send: Great social change brought great debate: Confucius, Laozi, Mencius, Zhuangzi, Mozi, Han Fei, Sun Wu… Thinkers wrote books and argued — the “Hundred Schools of Thought contending”.

clips.send: Lidui rock and Yulei Mountain. The rock left when the mountain was cut. Workers cut an opening through Yulei Mountain to lead water to the plain. The piece of mountain separated from the rest is called Lidui (the “separated mound”). With no explosives, people heated the rock with fire and then poured cold water on it so it cracked.

clips.send: Feisha Weir (Feishayan). Spills extra water and flushes sand into the Outer River. A low section of the levee between the two rivers, originally built of bamboo cages filled with pebbles. When the Inner River is too full, extra water spills over it back into the Outer River. The bend of the river throws sand and pebbles over the weir too, so the Inner River and the Bottle-Neck Channel do not silt up.

clips.send: About 256 BCE Li Bing, governor of Shu for the state of Qin, led the building of Dujiangyan on the Min River. The Chengdu Plain became “the Land of Abundance” — a rich rear base for Qin.

clips.send: Fish Mouth (Yuzui). Splits the Min River into the Inner and Outer River. Built in the middle of the Min River and shaped like a fish’s mouth. It divides the river: the Inner River (east) is for irrigation; the Outer River (west) is the main course and carries floods away. “Four–six split”: in the dry season about 60 percent of the water enters the Inner River; in the flood season only about 40 percent does.

clips.send: Bottle-Neck Channel (Baopingkou). Controls how much water enters the plain. A channel cut through Yulei Mountain; its narrow shape is like the neck of a bottle. However high the river rises, only a limited amount of water can pass through, so the plain gets steady water without floods. The canals beyond it spread water across the Chengdu Plain.

clips.send: 公元前 356 年，秦孝公任用商鞅变法：国家承认土地私有，允许自由买卖；奖励耕战，按军功授予爵位和田宅；建立县制，由国君直接派官吏治理。秦国成为战国后期最富强的国家。

clips.send: 离堆与玉垒山。 凿开玉垒山后分离出来的石堆。 人们在玉垒山上凿开一个口子，把水引向平原。 被分离出来的那块山体叫“离堆”。 当时没有火药，人们先用火烧岩石，再泼冷水，让岩石炸裂，再一点点开凿。

clips.send: 鱼嘴（分水堤）。 把岷江一分为二：内江和外江。 修在岷江江心，形状像鱼的嘴巴。 它把岷江分为内江和外江：内江（东）用于灌溉，外江（西）是岷江正流，主要用来排洪。 “四六分水”：枯水季节约六成江水进入内江；丰水季节只有约四成进入内江。

clips.send: 社会大变革带来了思想大活跃：孔子、老子、孟子、庄子、墨子、韩非、孙武……各派思想家著书立说、互相辩论，形成了“百家争鸣”的局面。

clips.send: 李冰。 战国时期秦国的蜀郡守。 战国时期（约公元前 256 年），秦国蜀郡守李冰主持修建了都江堰。 它是世界上至今仍在使用、以无坝引水为特征的最古老的水利工程之一。 它让秦国的后方富庶起来，为秦后来统一全国打下了基础。

clips.send: 公元前 230 年至前 221 年，秦王嬴政先后灭掉韩、赵、魏、楚、燕、齐六国，公元前 221 年完成统一。（秦朝的故事见下一单元。）

clips.send: 经过兼并战争，战国时期形成了齐、楚、燕、韩、赵、魏、秦七个强国，史称“战国七雄”。口诀：东齐南楚西方秦，北燕中间赵魏韩。

clips.send: 成都平原。 “天府之国”。 修建都江堰以前，成都平原常常发生水灾和旱灾。 都江堰建成后，成都平原“水旱从人”，成为“天府之国”。 都江堰已经使用了两千多年，2000 年（与青城山一起）被列入世界文化遗产。

clips.send: 外江（岷江正流）。 岷江正流，主要用来排洪。 外江河床较宽、较浅。 丰水季节水位高时，大部分江水（约六成）从外江排走，保护成都平原免受洪灾。

clips.send: 公元前 770 年，周平王东迁洛邑，东周开始。东周分为两个时期：春秋（前 770—前 476 年）和战国（前 475—前 221 年）。

clips.send: 春秋时期，周王室衰微，诸侯争当“霸主”。齐桓公任用管仲改革，以“尊王攘夷”为号召，成为春秋时期第一个霸主。此后，晋、楚、吴、越等国也相继争霸。

clips.send: 内江。 把江水引向成都平原，用于灌溉。 内江河床较深、较窄。 所以枯水季节水位低时，更多的水流进内江，保证了灌溉用水。 看看计数：枯水期内江约占六成。

clips.send: 飞沙堰。 泄洪、排沙。 内江和外江之间一段较低的堤堰，最初用竹笼装卵石筑成。 内江水量过大时，多余的水漫过飞沙堰流入外江，起到泄洪作用。 利用弯道水流，把泥沙、卵石甩过飞沙堰排入外江，防止内江和宝瓶口淤塞。

clips.send: 宝瓶口。 控制进入成都平原的水量。 在玉垒山上凿出的引水口，形状像瓶口。 不管江水涨得多高，能通过的水量都有限，成都平原因此得到稳定的灌溉用水，又不会被淹。 它后面的渠道把水分送到成都平原各地。
